answer: Pottery Decoration diversity and Pottery Form diversity first show opposite growth trends in the 18th century BCE (1800–1700 BCE): in that same century, Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz) increases significantly from −0.48 to +0.97 Z (Δ = +1.45 Z) while Pottery Form (ZKeform) declines simultaneously from +0.74 to −1.13 Z (Δ = −1.87 Z). This 1800→1700 BCE transition is the ONLY century in the entire 4300–500 BCE record (39 century-anchors, 38 transitions) in which the two diverge in opposite directions, and it is the earliest such occurrence in absolute time; both series then plateau (1700–1100 BCE), so no later century ever re-exhibits the opposite-trend pattern.

payload.hypothesis: The first century in which Pottery Decoration diversity rises significantly (+1.45 Z, from -0.48 to +0.97) while Pottery Form diversity declines simultaneously (-1.87 Z, from +0.74 to -1.13) is the 18th century BCE, i.e., 1800-1700 BCE - the unique opposite-trend bin across the whole 4300-500 BCE record.
payload.workflow: 1) Load capital.csv with comma-decimal parsing (decimal=','); confirm 39 century anchors at BCE 4300->500 (100-yr steps, no missing). 2) Map variables: ZKeform = Diversity in Pottery Form, Zkeverz = Diversity in Pottery Decoration (both Cultural Capital per study context); verify exact agreement (37/37 overlapping anchors) with raw PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration in time_series_data.csv. 3) Compute growth trend as chronological first difference between consecutive 100-yr bins. 4) Select bins where dForm<0 AND dDec>0 (simultaneous opposite trends). 5) Take the earliest qualifying bin in absolute time = first occurrence = 1800->1700 BCE. 6) Label the century as 18th century BCE (span 1800-1700 BCE). 7) Robustness: repeat with magnitude thresholds 0.0-1.2 Z (unchanged); cross-check the interpolated 1-yr series signs (identical); document the +0.0015 anchor-boundary interpolation artifact.
